elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Licensor may conduct such an audit no more than once in any 12-month period" — an express frequency cap on the Article V.IV(b) audit right, which previously had none.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "upon at least 30 days' prior written notice to Licensee." This is genuine advance notice to Customer, replacing the original sentence that merely gave Licensee 30 days to permit an audit after a request.
"Audits shall be conducted during Licensee's normal business hours..."

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Retained original: "an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional, (selected by mutual agreement)" — already met, correctly left untouched.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: "the auditor shall be bound by written confidentiality obligations".

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: "...and off-site where possible" in the inserted sentence.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained p0064: "The cost of the audit will be borne by Licensor unless a discrepancy of more than five-percent (5%) is discovered, in which case the cost of the audit shall be borne by Licensee." Licensor is the Vendor; threshold is exactly 5%.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: "neither Licensor nor the auditor shall have direct access to Licensee's systems." Scope of the audit remains limited to accounting records.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: "no more than once in any 12-month period" satisfies the once-per-year cap.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: 30 days' prior written notice exceeds the 15-day fallback minimum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: The retained cost sentence shifts cost to Licensee at a discrepancy of more than 5%, not 10%; read literally, Vendor ceases to bear cost below the 10% fallback threshold. Immaterial here because the preferred level (5%) is fully met.

reasons: Finding status "deviation" is correct: the original Article V.IV(b) contained no frequency cap and no advance-notice requirement (the original 30-day period ran against Licensee after a Licensor request), which is unlimited/unannounced audit territory and fails the fallback.

All eight preferred elements are met in the rendered operative language, so the redline is position-complete at the preferred level; the fallback cost element (10%) is literally unmet because the retained clause shifts cost at 5%, but that is the preferred threshold and does not affect completeness.

Minimality holds: two short edits only. The pre-existing independent-auditor/mutual-selection and 5% cost-shift language is retained verbatim; no survival tails, expense language, procedures or extraneous obligations were added. Deletion of the original sentence "Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor" is necessary rather than cosmetic, since a duty to permit within 30 days of the request would contradict the new 30-day prior-notice requirement; it was Vendor-favourable, not a Customer protection.

Intent is preserved: audit purpose (compliance with all terms), scope (appropriate accounting records), mutual auditor selection and the cost-allocation mechanic all survive without contradiction; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are introduced (Licensor/Licensee are defined parties).

Drafting note only, no repair required: consider aligning "discrepancy" with underpayment language if a future turn is taken, and confirm the third sentence is inserted into Article V.IV(b) rather than standing free, so its scope is unambiguously the audit right.
